chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A son whom a man precedes (in death) is superior to seventy sons whom he leaves behind after him, all of them having ridden the cavalry horses and fought in the Way of Allah.
ai.seo_question: Why is a son who dies before his parent considered superior to many surviving sons?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the unique spiritual status of a child who dies in childhood, emphasizing that their purity and lack of worldly burden grant them a higher rank than seventy adult martyrs. Scholars note that the comparison to seventy warriors highlights the exceptional merit of early death, as the child is spared the trials of life and the potential for sin, securing a direct path to Paradise. This concept reinforces the Shia emphasis on the intercession and high status of the Ahl al-Bayt's descendants and righteous children who pass away young.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazi’e, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A son who preceded the man (in dying) is superior than seventy sons left behind after him, all of them having ridden the cavalry horses and fought in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from ibn Bazi‘ from abu Isma’il al- Sarraj who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
a son whom one sends (to the next life) is better than seventy sons who survive after one’s death, who have mounted their horses and are ready to march for the cause of Allah.”
